title: If you are grateful
hookLine: if you are grateful I will surely increase you (14:7)
tomorrow: The good word, the good tree

lines: REMEMBER WHAT YOU WERE SAVED FROM.
cards: Surah fourteen is named for Ibrahim, but a few verses in, it's Musa who speaks. He tells his people, the Children of Israel: remember.
Remember God's favor when He saved you from Pharaoh's people, who tormented you and killed your sons. Then he passes on a sentence God Himself had proclaimed.
It's about a word you met on day eleven of this path, when you learned the difference between praise and thanks. Today, the thanks gets its own verse.

teach.h: IF YOU GIVE THANKS, I WILL GIVE MORE.
teach.b: Verse seven. In Pickthall's translation, your Lord proclaimed: "If ye give thanks, I will give you more". In Arabic: la'in shakartum la-azidannakum.
The grammar is emphatic, a promise with an oath folded in: if you are grateful, I will surely, surely increase you. And the other side: if you are ungrateful, the punishment is severe.

The word there is kafartum, from kufr. Its root means to cover, the way a farmer covers a seed with soil; another verse, 57:20, uses the same word for farmers. Ingratitude covers a gift up, as if it weren't there.
Shukr is the opposite. Classical scholars such as ar-Raghib describe it as showing a favor's effect, letting the gift be seen.
Al-Ghazali and others describe three parts: in the heart, recognizing the gift came from God; on the tongue, saying so; in the limbs, using the gift well. And people are included.
A hadith in Abu Dawud and at-Tirmidhi says: whoever does not thank people has not thanked God. Remember a name you met last year: ash-Shakur, the Appreciative, one of God's names in the Qur'an.
God, who needs nothing, is described as appreciating the small good people do, and multiplying it. So what is the increase?
Scholars read it widely: more of the blessing, more blessings, more of the gratitude itself, a heart that sees more.
They disagree about which, and some say all. What they share is the direction.
Gratitude doesn't just answer the gift. It grows it.

how: Muslims express shukr by saying alhamdulillah, by thanking people, and by using blessings well; some perform a prostration of thanks, sujud ash-shukr, on receiving good news.

o: gratitude: seeing a gift, saying so, using it well
praise of God for who He is, apart from any gift
a payment owed to God after good news arrives

games.q: inside the verse — tap the pairs.
p: gratitude, letting a gift be seen
covering, as soil covers a seed
the Grateful, a name of God

s: Surah Ibrahim's verse on gratitude is spoken by Ibrahim
Musa passes it on to his people, the Children of Israel (14:6–7).
one of God's names means the Grateful
ash-Shakur: God appreciates the small good people do and multiplies it.
thanking people has nothing to do with thanking God
a hadith says whoever doesn't thank people hasn't thanked God.

games.q: you've been saved from Pharaoh's people. your prophet tells you God has proclaimed something. what is it?
o: if you give thanks, I will give you more.
games.why: if you give thanks, I will surely increase you; and if you cover the gift up, the punishment is severe (14:7).

practice: Let three specific gifts come to mind: not my family, but the way your sister laughed on the phone yesterday.
Hold each for a few breaths and recognize it in your heart; if you pray, say alhamdulillah, or thank God in your own words. Then think how you might use one of them well, with your hands.

wordCard.voice: Shukr. Gratitude: recognizing a gift, saying so, and using it well. Its opposite, kufr, covers the gift up. Today's word.

orig.note: Arabic: gratitude, thanks; from sh-k-r, showing the effect of a favor.

carryVoice: Your line: gratitude grows it. In the heart, on the tongue, in the hands. See you tomorrow.

sources.q: If ye give thanks, I will give you more
